NS.source_note: Nova Scotia Student Assistance page for students with disabilities: 40% course load counts as full-time, extra funding for disability costs, Post-Secondary Accessibility Services partner.
211 Nova Scotia: free, confidential, 24/7; call or text 2-1-1.

Employment Nova Scotia interventions page; lists reachAbility workshops for unemployed Nova Scotians with disabilities. No better disability-specific official page found (dsp and dcs employment URLs 404).

NS.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
NS.name: Nova Scotia Legal Aid
NS.summary: Helps Nova Scotians with criminal, family or social justice issues, including income security; offers legal information, summary advice and lawyer representation. Free online chats cover CPP Disability.

NS.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
NS.name: Legal Information Society of Nova Scotia
NS.summary: Charitable non-profit giving Nova Scotians legal information and resources since 1982. Legally trained staff reachable by phone, email or live chat (information, not legal advice).

NS.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
NS.name: Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission
NS.summary: Independent government agency administering the NS Human Rights Act. Offers an online inquiry form and Know Your Rights resources.

NS.name: 211 Nova Scotia
NS.summary: Free, confidential, 24/7 service connecting people to community, government and social services. Call or text 2-1-1; live chat and email also available.

NS.name: Disability Alliance Canada
NS.summary: National organization (not NS-specific) offering free one-on-one advocate support for the Disability Tax Credit, CPP Disability and Canada Disability Benefit.

NS.name: Disability Planning Helpline (rdsp.com)
NS.summary: Free, nationwide (not NS-specific) Disability Planning Helpline that can help with disability-related topics including the RDSP.

NS.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
NS.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service
NS.summary: Law school clinic at Dalhousie's Schulich School of Law serving community members who have nowhere else to turn; has a Welfare Rights guide for people seeking income assistance in Nova Scotia.

NS.name: Independent Living Nova Scotia
NS.whatTheyDo: Offers programs and resources that help Nova Scotians with disabilities make their own decisions, remove barriers and build skills.

NS.name: Inclusion Nova Scotia
NS.whatTheyDo: Provincial non-profit supporting people with intellectual disabilities and their families to live included lives, with programs like Life Transitions and Individual & Family Support.

NS.name: Autism Nova Scotia
NS.whatTheyDo: Provides programs, services and advocacy for Autistic people, families and caregivers through regional centres across the province.

NS.name: Easter Seals Nova Scotia
NS.whatTheyDo: Runs Camp Tidnish, New Leaf Enterprises supported employment, Take PART recreation and an Assisted Mobility program for Nova Scotians with disabilities.

NS.name: reachAbility Association
NS.whatTheyDo: Non-profit offering free self-management and employment programs, plus training and consultation for employers.

NS.name: Spinal Cord Injury Nova Scotia
NS.whatTheyDo: Offers free, lifelong support to people with spinal cord injuries and other mobility disabilities, plus families and caregivers: counselling, advocacy, information, peer support and employment help.

NS.name: Society of Deaf and Hard of Hearing Nova Scotians
NS.whatTheyDo: Coordinates qualified sign language interpreters across the province and offers community services and accessibility resources for Deaf and hard of hearing Nova Scotians.
